title: Relational aperture transfer candidate for microscopic spatial-mode collapse
proposed_by: TECT research programme under operator directive
immutability: This accepted source file is immutable. Any mathematical change requires PAH-001-v2 or a new packet ID.

interpretive_boundary.inspiration: The intuition that spatial distinctions may cease to be operational beyond a horizon-like boundary is translated into two testable microscopic predicates: low-energy spatial-mode quotient collapse and directional trapped transfer.
interpretive_boundary.meaning_of_space_collapse: After gauge and symmetry zero modes are removed, all non-harmonic internal modes of a low-aperture component leave every fixed low-energy window, while a tagged local probe has vanishing outward transfer probability at fixed external time.

finite_regulator.carrier: G=(V,E,P) is a finite connected oriented bounded-degree two-cell complex with disjoint nonempty outer-readout anchor O and core anchor C; no embedding coordinates or Lorentzian metric are part of rho.
finite_regulator.dimension: finite relational two-cell complex; emergent spatial dimension is an output target and is not inserted
finite_regulator.matter_cutoff: M_psi>=1 with radial level ell_v in {0,...,M_psi} and |psi_v|=R_max ell_v/M_psi
finite_regulator.edge_scale: a>0 is a refinement label only; physical length is not identified
finite_regulator.volume: |V| finite; no physical volume interpretation is admitted
finite_regulator.degree_bound: deg_G(v)<=d_max with d_max fixed before regulator removal
finite_regulator.spatial_boundary_condition: the finite anchored complex and its incidence data are fixed; O and C are labels, not imposed field values
finite_regulator.time_boundary_condition: stationary initial-value Markov law on t>=0 with initial distribution pi_(rho,Q), right-continuous paths, and no terminal conditioning
finite_regulator.normalization: counting measure on the fixed-Q finite configuration space and Z_(rho,Q)=sum_x exp(-beta F_rho(x))
finite_regulator.finite_parts: none beyond the displayed finite functional; additive constants are fixed by the displayed formula
finite_regulator.common_norm: supremum norm on bounded gauge- and anchor-automorphism-invariant cylinder observables
finite_regulator.parameter_domain: beta>0, nu>0, R_max>0, lambda_s>0, eta_6>0, kappa_s>0, kappa_D>0, kappa_g>0, g>0; m2 and lambda_4 are real inserted parameters; every rate scale is positive and frozen before any comparison

microscopic_degrees_of_freedom.aperture: s_v on the finite aperture grid in [epsilon,1]
microscopic_degrees_of_freedom.matter: psi_v=(R_max ell_v/M_psi) zeta_K^(n_v), with n_v in Z_K and sum_v ell_v=Q
microscopic_degrees_of_freedom.link: U_e in Z_K on each oriented edge, with U_(bar e)=U_e^(-1)
microscopic_degrees_of_freedom.probe: an optional neutral tagged probe X in V used only by the preregistered transfer estimand
microscopic_degrees_of_freedom.configuration_space: Omega_(rho,Q) is the finite set of all displayed variables satisfying the fixed-Q and edge-reversal constraints

symmetry_and_constraint.gauge_action: psi_v -> zeta_K^(g_v) psi_v and U_(v,w) -> zeta_K^(g_w) U_(v,w) zeta_K^(-g_v); aperture and probe labels are neutral
symmetry_and_constraint.relabelling_group: the finite automorphism group Aut(G;O,C) preserving the cell incidence and both anchors
symmetry_and_constraint.fixed_sector: Q=sum_v ell_v is fixed within one finite comparison
symmetry_and_constraint.candidate_internal_projection: P_cand=P_Aut P_G, the finite group average on L2(Omega_(rho,Q),pi_(rho,Q))
symmetry_and_constraint.projection_boundary: P_cand is only the candidate's finite gauge and relabelling projection; it is not the TECT physical sector, a diffeomorphism quotient, or a QFT Gauss-law theorem

functional_or_action.name: F_rho
functional_or_action.plaquette_stiffness: J_p(s)=|boundary p|^(-1) sum_(e in boundary p) J_e(s)
functional_or_action.plaquette_holonomy: U_p is the ordered product of U_e around the oriented boundary of p
functional_or_action.formula: F_rho=sum_v[lambda_s(s_v-1)^2/2+m2|psi_v|^2/2+lambda_4|psi_v|^4/4+eta_6|psi_v|^6/6+g s_v^2|psi_v|^2/2]+kappa_s sum_(e=(v,w))(s_v-s_w)^2/2+kappa_D sum_(e=(v,w))J_e(s)|psi_w-U_e psi_v|^2/2+kappa_g sum_p J_p(s)(1-Re U_p)
functional_or_action.measure_and_jacobian: finite counting measure; no continuum Jacobian is inserted
functional_or_action.sign_convention: lower F_rho has larger Gibbs weight exp(-beta F_rho)
functional_or_action.boundedness: Omega_(rho,Q) is finite and epsilon>0, so F_rho and Z_(rho,Q) are finite for every admitted finite regulator

move_set: matter phase increment or decrement at one vertex
one radial occupation quantum transferred across one edge, preserving Q
one link multiplied by zeta_K or zeta_K^(-1)
one aperture grid step at one vertex
dynamics.inverse_pair_rule: Every move r has an explicit inverse r^(-1).
dynamics.time: t is external stochastic time; local clock accumulation is d tau_v=s_v^nu dt
dynamics.thermal_boundary: beta defines the finite reversible state; no quantum KMS or proper-time identity is inferred
dynamics.finite_transfer_target: T_rho(t) is positivity preserving, fixes 1, is reversible in L2(pi), and satisfies ||T_rho(t)f||_infinity<=||f||_infinity
dynamics.dynamics_selection_boundary: nu, every move, and every rate scale are inserted dynamics data and cannot be selected from a static fit

horizon_collapse_tests.low_aperture_region: I_(epsilon_c) is the connected component containing C in the induced subcomplex {v:s_v<=epsilon_c}, with O disjoint from I_(epsilon_c)
horizon_collapse_tests.covariant_incidence: (D_U phi)_e=phi_w-U_e phi_v on oriented edges internal to I_(epsilon_c)
horizon_collapse_tests.spectral_collapse_predicate: For every fixed Lambda<infinity, Tr 1_[0,Lambda](K_I) -> dim ker(D_U|_I); equivalently the first eigenvalue above ker(D_U|_I) diverges after gauge and symmetry zero modes are removed.
horizon_collapse_tests.sufficient_uniform_target: If gamma_I is the first positive eigenvalue of D_U^*D_U, prove gamma_I/epsilon_c -> infinity along the declared sequence; then every fixed non-harmonic low-energy window empties.
horizon_collapse_tests.topology_boundary: Nontrivial holonomy or additional harmonic modes are counted as surviving topology and are not forced into one collective mode.
horizon_collapse_tests.probe_rates: For each oriented active edge v->w, k(v->w)=kappa_0 s_v^nu.
horizon_collapse_tests.outward_predicate: p_out(rho,T)=sup_(v in I) P_v(tau_O<=T) <= d_max kappa_0 T epsilon_c^nu, hence p_out->0 for fixed T if epsilon_c->0.
horizon_collapse_tests.inward_predicate: For an exterior vertex x with s_x>=s_0>0 and at least one edge into I, preregister p_in(T_0)>=c_0 where c_0=(s_0^nu/d_max)(1-exp(-kappa_0 s_0^nu T_0))>0.
horizon_collapse_tests.joint_acceptance: Both the spectral-collapse and trapped-transfer predicates must pass under one regulator sequence; neither implies the other.
horizon_collapse_tests.limit_order_firewall: epsilon_c->0 is taken before T_obs->infinity; reversing this order is a different proposition and normally removes finite-time trapping.

assumptions: Each finite regulator satisfies the displayed carrier, cutoff, orientation and fixed-Q constraints.
Every local move and its inverse are enumerated before a run, and the mobility symmetry is part of the source definition.
The aperture variable is microscopic clock/coupling data, not an already reconstructed lapse or metric component.
The two collapse predicates are logically independent and must be tested on the same regulator sequence.
Any future Reading-H comparison retains the existing same-owner scope lock and does not compare different Q sectors or ensembles.
missing_assumptions: A primary and independent proof of finite gauge invariance, detailed balance, transfer positivity, projection commutation and finite stability.
An admitted stationary low-aperture branch and same-Q high-aperture reference under one scope fingerprint.
A proof that the declared refinement embeddings give one invariant common core and that boundary defects vanish there.
Uniform lower control of gamma_I/epsilon_c and a volume-independent exterior causal-influence envelope.
Uniform cutoff, lattice, volume, exhaustion, selector, aperture and beta estimates in the declared order.
A Lorentzian reconstruction and causal map that could distinguish an event horizon from apparent, trapping or Cauchy boundaries.
A complete F_lim, F_eff and F_obs map with uncertainty, nuisance, immutable scorer and prospective holdout.
Independent evidence that the candidate corresponds to the observed universe rather than only a mathematical model.

falsifiers.test: finite gauge invariance, detailed balance, transfer positivity or projection commutation
falsifiers.failure: reject this candidate version before finite admission
reject the finite model if F_rho or Z_(rho,Q) is not well-defined
reject spatial-mode collapse if gamma_I/epsilon_c fails to diverge or unaccounted low modes survive
reject trapped transfer if p_out lacks a uniform epsilon power bound or p_in also vanishes
reject the horizon-like proposition if it requires T_obs->infinity before epsilon->0 or an undeclared interchange
reject the candidate sequence if the result depends on arbitrary labels or incompatible refinement choices
withhold every causal or Lorentzian interpretation if no volume-independent exterior propagation envelope exists
report a surviving mobility equivalence class if static-equivalent nu or rates change the two-time estimand
reject the branch if it disappears when the selector is removed after volume/exhaustion
reject only this candidate branch if Delta F is nonnegative, error-overlapping, scheme-dependent, nonstationary or transversely unstable
retain only finite evidence if generator agreement or boundary-defect decay fails on A_cyl^inv
do not identify Pre-A, GR or an event horizon if the effective and observational maps remain undefined or fail holdout validation
